findings: The original graph passes CPU checks for 151210848 components. The first two NPU attempts fail in the harness because the NPU execution-device property is a string, while CPU returns a list. Both are normalized without weakening explicit-device validation.

The first actual NPU inference fails UNORM rounding: color [0.5,0.25,0.75,1] becomes [127,63,191,255] rather than [128,64,191,255]. Applying an integer byte mask before deriving the fractional remainder preserves the rounding increment. This follows the existing qualified solid-rectangle graph structure.
The corrected NPU graph passes all eight image/format cases and every output component, including adjacent floats around selected half-byte rounding boundaries. Failed graph variants are retained.
Registered-driver CPU build work overlaps these calls, so timing is diagnostic and not an isolated performance comparison. No driver clear callback or live desktop clear has used this graph yet.
